$S(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$ is real for $q>2^{1/3}\approx1.26$ and it is economic, $S(q)\ge0$, only for

$S(q_{0})=0\iff q_{0}^{3}=3$, $q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$.

For $q<q_{0}$ the inverse supply is negative and for $q<2^{1/3}$ it is not real at all, so extending the supply integral to $0$ is a purely formal continuation. The economically relevant producer surplus is

$PS^{*}= \int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P^{*}-S(q)\big]dq
      =P^{*}\big(Q^{*}-q_{0}\big)-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq$,

and the conventional consumer surplus is

$CS^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*}$,

$D(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$.

Hence the net market surplus measured from the zero-price point is

$W_{net}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
          =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq-P^{*}q_{0}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
          =\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[D(q)-S(q)\big]dq+\int_{0}^{q_{0}}D(q)dq-P^{*}q_{0}$.

Numerically

$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq =18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx32.4$–$32.5$,

with the refinement used here $I_{D}\approx32.47$.

$\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.8$–$9.9$,
about $9.88$ on a Simpson mesh with $h=0.25$ on $[q_{0},Q^{*}]$.

$P^{*}q_{0}\approx4.62\times1.442\approx6.66$.

Therefore

$CS^{*}=I_{D}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.47-4.62\times4.69\approx10.8$,

$PS^{*}=P^{*}(Q^{*}-q_{0})-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S\approx4.62(4.69-1.44)-9.88\approx5.0$–$5.2$,

and

$W_{net}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
           \approx I_{D}-P^{*}q_{0}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S
           \approx32.47-6.66-9.88\approx15.9$–$16.0$.

That is $CS^{*}\approx10.8$ and $PS^{*}\approx5.1$, i.e. $\approx15.9$ units of total surplus, the area between demand and the economic part of supply from $q_{0}=3^{1/3}$ to $Q^{*}$ plus the demand triangle below $q_{0}$.

The often quoted $\approx22$–$23$ figure is $W_{g}^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S$, i.e. $CS^{*}+PS^{*}+P^{*}q_{0}$. It includes the rectangular term $P^{*}q_{0}\approx6.7$ which is the inframarginal value of the $q_{0}$ units that would be supplied at zero price and is normally removed when producer surplus is defined from the zero-price point. On the economically relevant interval $[q_{0},Q^{*}]$ the between-curves surplus is $\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}[D-S]dq\approx7.3$–$7.5$, consistent with $CS_{net}\approx5.6$ and $PS_{net}\approx1.7$ after the $P^{*}q_{0}$ normalisation.

With the $q_{0}$ normalisation the competitive total welfare at $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ is therefore $\approx15.9$–$16.0$, essentially the $15$–$16$ total surplus quoted by the $q_{0}$-normalised calculation.

5.text:
The inverse market is

$$P_{S}(Q)=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right), \qquad 
P_{D}(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q},\qquad Q^{3}>2 ,$$

so that on the admissible branch

$$f(Q):= \ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0$$

is the market clearing condition.  $f'(Q)=3Q^{2}/(Q^{3}-2)+
18e^{-\arctan Q}/(1+Q^{2})>0$ on $Q>2^{1/3}$, so the root is unique.
$f(4.6)<0<f(4.7)$ and

$$Q^{*}\approx4.69\!-\!4.70\approx4.69 ,\qquad
P^{*}= \ln\!\left({Q^{*}}^{3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx4.6\!-\!4.7,
$$

in particular

$$Q^{*}\simeq4.69,\qquad P^{*}\simeq\ln(101.1)\simeq4.62 ,$$

is the competitive $MB=MC$ pair, $P^{*}Q^{*}\simeq4.62\times4.69\simeq
21.6\!-\!21.7$.

Put $D(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$ and $S(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$.  On the
economically relevant part $S(q)=0$ at

$$Q_{0}:\;S(Q_{0})=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}=3,\qquad Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.44,$$

the Marshallian surpluses are

$$CS^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*},\qquad
PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq ,$$

so that the gross surplus between the two inverse curves up to $Q^{*}$ is

$$W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
       =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
       =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[\,D(q)-S_{e}(q)\,\big]dq ,$$

$S_{e}\equiv0$ for $q<Q_{0}$.

Numerically

$$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq
   =18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq
   \approx 32.4\!-\!32.6\approx 32.5,$$

$$\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
   =\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
   \approx 9.8\!-\!9.9\approx 9.9,$$

so that with the quoted root

$$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 21.69,\qquad
CS^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 32.47-21.69\approx10.8,$$

$$PS^{*}_{g}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S\approx21.69-9.93\approx11.8,$$

and

$$W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}_{g}
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
      \approx 32.5-9.9\approx 22\!-\!23, $$

about $W_{g}^{*}\simeq22.5\!-\!22.9$, e.g. $W_{g}^{*}\approx22.6$ for
$Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$.  This is $CS^{*}\approx\$10.8$
and a gross producer surplus $\approx\$11.8$, i.e. the usual
$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}[P_{D}-P_{S}]dq$ area between demand and inverse
supply at the competitive equilibrium.

Remark on normalisation.  The $P^{*}Q_{0}\approx6.67$ rectangle is often
removed when producer surplus is measured net of the zero-price
threshold $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}$.  In the $Q_{0}$-normalised convention

$$PS_{net}^{*}=P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\right)-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S
          \approx5.1\!-\!5.6,\qquad
W_{net}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{net}^{*}
          =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D-P^{*}Q_{0}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S
          \approx15\!-\!16\approx15.9,$$

which is $W_{g}^{*}-P^{*}Q_{0}$.  The formal integral
$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq$ diverges at $q_{m}=2^{1/3}$ because
$\ln(q^{3}-2)\to-\infty$, so the finite Marshallian numbers above are
the conventional ones.  This is the $Q^{*}\approx4.7$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$
competitive equilibrium of the $\ln(Q^{3}-2)$ supply / $18e^{-\arctan Q}$
demand system.

8.text:
The inverse curves can be written on the same price scale

$$P_{S}(q)=\ln \!\big(q^{3}-2\big),\qquad 
P_{D}(q)=18\,e^{-\arctan q},\qquad q^{3}>2,
$$

so that the competitive price is the unique root of

$$f(q)=\ln \!\big(q^{3}-2\big)-18e^{-\arctan q}=0 ,\qquad 
f'(q)=\frac{3q^{2}}{q^{3}-2}+\frac{18e^{-\arctan q}}{1+q^{2}}>0,
$$

on the admissible branch.  $f(4.6)<0<f(4.7)$ and Newton iteration gives

$$Q^{*}\approx 4.69\!-\!4.70\approx 4.69,\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln\!\big(Q^{*3}-2\big)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx 4.6\!-\!4.7,
$$

in particular $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$, $P^{*}Q^{*}\simeq
21.6\!-\!21.7$.  This is the market clearing $MB=MC$ point.

Put $D(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$ and $S(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$.  On the
economically relevant part $S(q)=0$ at

$$q_{0}=S^{-1}(0)=3^{1/3}\approx1.442,
$$

and with the usual $S_{e}=0$ extension for $q<q_{0}$

\begin{align*}
I_{D}(Q^{*})&=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq
           =18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx 32.4\!-\!32.6\approx32.5,\\
I_{S}(Q^{*})&=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
           =\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\big(q^{3}-2\big)dq\approx 9.8\!-\!9.9 .
\end{align*}

Hence in the conventional Marshallian notation

$$CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 32.5-21.7\approx10.8\!-\!11.0, $$

$$PS_{g}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}(Q^{*})\approx21.7-9.9\approx11.8\!-\!12.0, $$

and the gross social surplus, i.e. the area between demand and the
extended supply $S_{e}$ up to $Q^{*}$,

$$W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{g}^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-I_{S}(Q^{*})
       =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
       \approx 32.5-9.9\approx 22\!-\!23, $$

about $W_{g}^{*}\simeq22.5\!-\!22.9$, $CS^{*}\simeq10.8$ and
$PS_{g}^{*}\simeq11.8$ for $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$.
In closed form

$$W_{g}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq-
       \int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\big(q^{3}-2\big)dq,\qquad
\ln\!\big(Q^{*3}-2\big)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}, $$

which is $\approx 22.6$ on the quoted numerical root.

Remark on normalisation.  With the textbook net producer surplus
$PS_{net}=P^{*}(Q^{*}-q_{0})-I_{S}(Q^{*})$ the $P^{*}q_{0}\approx6.67$
rectangle is removed and

$$W_{net}=CS^{*}+PS_{net}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}q_{0}-I_{S}(Q^{*})
       \approx15\!-\!16\approx15.9,$$

$CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS_{net}\approx5.1$, the usual $Q_{0}$-normalised
area $\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}[D(q)-S(q)]dq$ between the two curves on the
economically relevant interval $[q_{0},Q^{*}]$.  The $W_{g}\approx
22\!-\!23$ figure above is $W_{net}+P^{*}q_{0}$ and is the gross
$CS+PS$ normally quoted for the $P_{S}=\ln(q^{3}-2)$,
$P_{D}=18e^{-\arctan q}$ market. ∎

14.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the equilibrium root that everyone is converging on. 
$P_{S}= \ln(Q^{3}-2)$ and $P_{D}=18e^{-\arctan Q}$ give

$\ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}$

which is monotone for $Q>2^{1/3}$ and

$Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}= \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.62$

is the unique market clearing pair. The demand integral is robust,

$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq =18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx32.4\!-\!32.5$,

so $CS = \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.66\approx10.8$ is solid.

The disagreement is where producer surplus starts. $P_{S}(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$ is
negative for $q<Q_{0}$ with $P_{S}(Q_{0})=0$, $Q_{0}^{3}=3$, $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$,
and it diverges to $-\infty$ at $q_{m}=2^{1/3}\approx1.26$. There is no economic
supply for $q<Q_{0}$ and the formal integral $\int_{q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$ is not
an economic surplus.

The Marshallian producer surplus is measured from the zero-price point:

$PS^{*}= \int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P^{*}-P_{S}(q)\big]dq
       =P^{*}\big(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\big)-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq,$

and

$\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq =\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.8\!-\!9.9$

on the usual Simpson quadrature. Hence

$PS^{*}\approx P^{*}(4.69-1.442)-9.9\approx4.62\times3.248-9.9\approx5.0\!-\!5.3,$

about $5.1$ in the normalisation used by Colleagues 2 and 3.

Total welfare on the economically relevant interval is therefore

$W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-P^{*}Q_{0}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}dq-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}dq-P^{*}Q_{0}
      \approx32.5-9.9-6.66\approx15.9,$

i.e. $CS^{*}\approx10.8$ and $PS^{*}\approx5.1$, $W^{*}\approx15\!-\!16$.

The $ \approx22\!-\!23$ figure that is quoted as $CS+PS$ is the gross area
$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}dq-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}dq$, i.e. $CS+PS+P^{*}Q_{0}$.
It adds the rectangle $P^{*}Q_{0}\approx6.67$ which is the inframarginal
revenue under $P^{*}$ from $0$ to $Q_{0}$ where marginal cost is negative and
supply is economically meaningless. Once the supply is truncated at the zero-price
point $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}$, the conventional net surplus between the two curves is
$\approx15.9$, the $ \approx10.8$ consumer surplus plus the $\approx5.1$ producer
surplus measured from $S=0$. That is the textbook $CS+PS$ welfare for the
given $ \ln(Q^{3}-2)$ supply.

The inverse market is

$$P_{S}(Q)=\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right),\qquad 
P_{D}(Q)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q},\qquad Q^{3}>2 ,$$

and the competitive price is the unique root of

$$f(Q)=\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0,
\qquad f'(Q)=\frac{3Q^{2}}{Q^{3}-2}+\frac{18e^{-\arctan Q}}{1+Q^{2}}>0,
$$

on the admissible branch.  Numerically

$$f(4.6)<0<f(4.7)$$

and

$$Q^{*}\approx 4.69\!-\!4.70\;,\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx4.6\!-\!4.7,
$$

in particular

$$Q^{*}\simeq 4.69,\qquad P^{*}\simeq4.62,\qquad 
P^{*}Q^{*}\simeq 21.6\!-\!21.7 ,
$$

is the $MB=MC$ price–quantity pair.  Put
$D(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$ and $S(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$ and $Q_{0}:S(Q_{0})=0$,
$Q_{0}^{3}=3$, $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$.  
In closed form

$$CS^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*},$$

$$PS_{g}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq,
$$

so that the gross Marshallian surplus is

$$W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{g}^{*}
        =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq .
$$

With $t=\arctan q$

$$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq
   =18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq
   =18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt
   \approx 32.4\!-\!32.5  ,
$$

and

$$\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
   =\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
   \approx 9.8\!-\!9.9\approx 9.9 .$$

Hence on the usual $P_{S}=0$ base

$$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.62\times4.69\approx21.7,$$

$$CS^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D-P^{*}Q^{*}
       \approx32.5-21.7\approx10.8,$$

$$PS_{g}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S
          \approx21.7-9.9\approx11.8,$$

and

$$W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{g}^{*}
        \approx\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S
        \approx32.5-9.9\approx22\!-\!23,$$

about $W_{g}^{*}\simeq22.5\!-\!22.8$, $CS^{*}\simeq10.8$, 
$PS_{g}^{*}\simeq11.8$, at $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$.
With the real domain $q_{m}=2^{1/3}$ the supply integral is
$\int_{q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}S\approx9.68\!-\!9.69$ and
$W_{m}^{*}\approx32.46-9.69\approx22.7\!-\!22.8$, i.e. the familiar
$\approx\$23$ gross $CS+PS$ surplus.

Remark on normalisation.  The net producer surplus measured from the
zero-price point is $PS_{net}=P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S\approx5.1$,
so that the $Q_{0}$-normalised total surplus

$$W_{net}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{net}
          =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D-P^{*}Q_{0}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S
          \approx15\!-\!16,$$

about $15.9$, is obtained.  $W_{g}^{*}=W_{net}^{*}+P^{*}Q_{0}$ recovers the
conventional gross $\approx22\!-\!23$ figure quoted above. ∎

is the unique competitive price-quantity. That part is not in dispute.

Where the welfare number changes is the baseline on which producer surplus is measured.  
$S(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$ is real for $q>2^{1/3}\approx1.26$ and it is economic, $S(q)\ge0$, only for

$S(q_{0})=0\iff q_{0}^{3}=3$, $q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$.

For $q<q_{0}$ the inverse supply is negative and for $q<2^{1/3}$ it is not real at all, so extending the supply integral to $0$ is a purely formal continuation. The economically relevant producer surplus is

$PS^{*}= \int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P^{*}-S(q)\big]dq
      =P^{*}\big(Q^{*}-q_{0}\big)-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq$,

and the conventional consumer surplus is

$CS^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*}$,

$D(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$.

Hence the net market surplus measured from the zero-price point is

$W_{net}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
          =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq-P^{*}q_{0}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
          =\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[D(q)-S(q)\big]dq+\int_{0}^{q_{0}}D(q)dq-P^{*}q_{0}$.

Numerically

$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq =18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx32.4$–$32.5$,

with the refinement used here $I_{D}\approx32.47$.

$\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.8$–$9.9$,
about $9.88$ on a Simpson mesh with $h=0.25$ on $[q_{0},Q^{*}]$.

$P^{*}q_{0}\approx4.62\times1.442\approx6.66$.

Therefore

$CS^{*}=I_{D}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.47-4.62\times4.69\approx10.8$,

$PS^{*}=P^{*}(Q^{*}-q_{0})-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S\approx4.62(4.69-1.44)-9.88\approx5.0$–$5.2$,

and

$W_{net}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
           \approx I_{D}-P^{*}q_{0}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S
           \approx32.47-6.66-9.88\approx15.9$–$16.0$.

That is $CS^{*}\approx10.8$ and $PS^{*}\approx5.1$, i.e. $\approx15.9$ units of total surplus, the area between demand and the economic part of supply from $q_{0}=3^{1/3}$ to $Q^{*}$ plus the demand triangle below $q_{0}$.

The often quoted $\approx22$–$23$ figure is $W_{g}^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S$, i.e. $CS^{*}+PS^{*}+P^{*}q_{0}$. It includes the rectangular term $P^{*}q_{0}\approx6.7$ which is the inframarginal value of the $q_{0}$ units that would be supplied at zero price and is normally removed when producer surplus is defined from the zero-price point. On the economically relevant interval $[q_{0},Q^{*}]$ the between-curves surplus is $\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}[D-S]dq\approx7.3$–$7.5$, consistent with $CS_{net}\approx5.6$ and $PS_{net}\approx1.7$ after the $P^{*}q_{0}$ normalisation.

With the $q_{0}$ normalisation the competitive total welfare at $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ is therefore $\approx15.9$–$16.0$, essentially the $15$–$16$ total surplus quoted by the $q_{0}$-normalised calculation.

The inverse market is

$$P_{S}(Q)=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right), \qquad 
P_{D}(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q},\qquad Q^{3}>2 ,$$

so that on the admissible branch

$$f(Q):= \ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0$$

is the market clearing condition.  $f'(Q)=3Q^{2}/(Q^{3}-2)+
18e^{-\arctan Q}/(1+Q^{2})>0$ on $Q>2^{1/3}$, so the root is unique.
$f(4.6)<0<f(4.7)$ and

$$Q^{*}\approx4.69\!-\!4.70\approx4.69 ,\qquad
P^{*}= \ln\!\left({Q^{*}}^{3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx4.6\!-\!4.7,
$$

in particular

$$Q^{*}\simeq4.69,\qquad P^{*}\simeq\ln(101.1)\simeq4.62 ,$$

is the competitive $MB=MC$ pair, $P^{*}Q^{*}\simeq4.62\times4.69\simeq
21.6\!-\!21.7$.

Put $D(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$ and $S(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$.  On the
economically relevant part $S(q)=0$ at

$$Q_{0}:\;S(Q_{0})=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}=3,\qquad Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.44,$$

the Marshallian surpluses are

$$CS^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*},\qquad
PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq ,$$

so that the gross surplus between the two inverse curves up to $Q^{*}$ is

$$W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
       =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
       =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[\,D(q)-S_{e}(q)\,\big]dq ,$$

$S_{e}\equiv0$ for $q<Q_{0}$.

Numerically

$$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq
   =18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq
   \approx 32.4\!-\!32.6\approx 32.5,$$

$$\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
   =\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
   \approx 9.8\!-\!9.9\approx 9.9,$$

so that with the quoted root

$$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 21.69,\qquad
CS^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 32.47-21.69\approx10.8,$$

$$PS^{*}_{g}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S\approx21.69-9.93\approx11.8,$$

and

$$W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}_{g}
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
      \approx 32.5-9.9\approx 22\!-\!23, $$

about $W_{g}^{*}\simeq22.5\!-\!22.9$, e.g. $W_{g}^{*}\approx22.6$ for
$Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$.  This is $CS^{*}\approx\$10.8$
and a gross producer surplus $\approx\$11.8$, i.e. the usual
$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}[P_{D}-P_{S}]dq$ area between demand and inverse
supply at the competitive equilibrium.

Remark on normalisation.  The $P^{*}Q_{0}\approx6.67$ rectangle is often
removed when producer surplus is measured net of the zero-price
threshold $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}$.  In the $Q_{0}$-normalised convention

$$PS_{net}^{*}=P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\right)-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S
          \approx5.1\!-\!5.6,\qquad
W_{net}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{net}^{*}
          =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D-P^{*}Q_{0}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S
          \approx15\!-\!16\approx15.9,$$

which is $W_{g}^{*}-P^{*}Q_{0}$.  The formal integral
$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq$ diverges at $q_{m}=2^{1/3}$ because
$\ln(q^{3}-2)\to-\infty$, so the finite Marshallian numbers above are
the conventional ones.  This is the $Q^{*}\approx4.7$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$
competitive equilibrium of the $\ln(Q^{3}-2)$ supply / $18e^{-\arctan Q}$
demand system.

I agree with the equilibrium root that everyone is converging on. 
$P_{S}= \ln(Q^{3}-2)$ and $P_{D}=18e^{-\arctan Q}$ give

$\ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}$

which is monotone for $Q>2^{1/3}$ and

$Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}= \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.62$

is the unique market clearing pair. The demand integral is robust,

$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq =18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx32.4\!-\!32.5$,

so $CS = \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.66\approx10.8$ is solid.

The disagreement is where producer surplus starts. $P_{S}(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$ is
negative for $q<Q_{0}$ with $P_{S}(Q_{0})=0$, $Q_{0}^{3}=3$, $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$,
and it diverges to $-\infty$ at $q_{m}=2^{1/3}\approx1.26$. There is no economic
supply for $q<Q_{0}$ and the formal integral $\int_{q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$ is not
an economic surplus.

The Marshallian producer surplus is measured from the zero-price point:

$PS^{*}= \int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P^{*}-P_{S}(q)\big]dq
       =P^{*}\big(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\big)-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq,$

and

$\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq =\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.8\!-\!9.9$

on the usual Simpson quadrature. Hence

$PS^{*}\approx P^{*}(4.69-1.442)-9.9\approx4.62\times3.248-9.9\approx5.0\!-\!5.3,$

about $5.1$ in the normalisation used by Colleagues 2 and 3.

Total welfare on the economically relevant interval is therefore

$W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-P^{*}Q_{0}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}dq-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}dq-P^{*}Q_{0}
      \approx32.5-9.9-6.66\approx15.9,$

i.e. $CS^{*}\approx10.8$ and $PS^{*}\approx5.1$, $W^{*}\approx15\!-\!16$.

The $ \approx22\!-\!23$ figure that is quoted as $CS+PS$ is the gross area
$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}dq-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}dq$, i.e. $CS+PS+P^{*}Q_{0}$.
It adds the rectangle $P^{*}Q_{0}\approx6.67$ which is the inframarginal
revenue under $P^{*}$ from $0$ to $Q_{0}$ where marginal cost is negative and
supply is economically meaningless. Once the supply is truncated at the zero-price
point $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}$, the conventional net surplus between the two curves is
$\approx15.9$, the $ \approx10.8$ consumer surplus plus the $\approx5.1$ producer
surplus measured from $S=0$. That is the textbook $CS+PS$ welfare for the
given $ \ln(Q^{3}-2)$ supply.

The inverse market is on the same price scale

$$P_{S}(q)=\ln \!\left(q^{3}-2\right),\qquad 
P_{D}(q)=18e^{-\arctan q},\qquad q^{3}>2, $$

and the competitive pair is the unique admissible root of

$$f(Q)=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0,\qquad 
f'(Q)=\frac{3Q^{2}}{Q^{3}-2}+\frac{18e^{-\arctan Q}}{1+Q^{2}}>0 .
$$

$f(4.6)<0<f(4.7)$ and

* $Q^{*}\simeq4.69\!-\!4.70$, $Q^{*}\approx4.69$,
* $P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.61\!-\!4.64$,
  $P^{*}\approx4.62$,

$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.62\times4.69\approx21.6\!-\!21.7$, the $MB=MC$ pair.

Let $Q_{0}$ be the zero-price of the inverse supply

$$P_{S}(Q_{0})=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}=3,\qquad Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\simeq1.442,
\qquad q_{m}=2^{1/3}\simeq1.260 .
$$

With $t=\arctan q$

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq
      =18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq
      =18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt
      \approx32.4\!-\!32.6\approx32.5 $$

is the total willingness to pay, and on the economic part of the
supply

$$I_{S}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
      =\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
      \approx9.8\!-\!9.9\approx9.9, $$

$\int_{q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}\approx9.68\!-\!9.69$.  Hence on the usual
Marshallian gross normalisation

$$CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!10.9\approx10.8,$$

$$PS_{g}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
          \approx21.7-9.9\approx11.7\!-\!12.0\approx11.8,$$

and the gross social surplus, i.e. the area between demand and the
$P_{S}=0$ extended supply up to $Q^{*}$,

$$W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{g}^{*}
        =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
        \approx32.5-9.9\approx22\!-\!23, $$

about $W_{g}^{*}\simeq22.5\!-\!22.9$, $W_{g}^{*}\approx22.6\!-\!22.8$
with $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$, $CS^{*}\approx\$10.8$,

$$W_{m}^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-\int_{q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}\approx32.46-9.69\approx22.7\!-\!22.8,$$

the familiar $\sim \$22\!-\!23$ total $CS+PS$ quoted for the
$\ln(q^{3}-2)$ / $18e^{-\arctan q}$ market.

Remark on normalisation.  The net producer surplus measured from the
zero-price point is

$$PS_{net}^{*}=P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}

$CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS_{net}^{*}\approx5.1$, is the same area with the

          \approx4.62\,(4.69-1.442)-9.9\approx5.0\!-\!5.3\approx5.1,$$

12.text:
Inverse supply and inverse demand are put on the same price scale

$$P_{S}(q)=\ln \left(q^{3}-2\right),\qquad 
P_{D}(q)=18e^{-\arctan q},\qquad q^{3}>2 ,$$

and the competitive price is the unique admissible root of

$$f(Q)=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0,
\qquad 
f'(Q)=\frac{3Q^{2}}{Q^{3}-2}+\frac{18e^{-\arctan Q}}{1+Q^{2}}>0 .
$$

$f(4.6)<0<f(4.7)$ and a Newton/bisection gives the familiar

$$Q^{*}\simeq4.69\!-\!4.70\approx4.69,\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.61\!-\!4.64
\approx4.62,$$

$$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.62\times4.69\approx21.6\!-\!21.7 .$$

The zero price of the inverse supply is

$$P_{S}(Q_{0})=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}=3,
\qquad Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442,
$$

$q_{m}=2^{1/3}\approx1.26$ being the formal real domain of the log.
Put $D(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$, $S(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$.

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq
      =18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq
      =18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt
      \approx 32.4\!-\!32.6\approx32.5, $$

$$I_{S}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
      =\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
      \approx9.8\!-\!9.9\approx9.9,
\qquad 
\int_{q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}S\approx9.68\!-\!9.69 .$$

In the usual Marshallian gross normalisation

$$
CS^{*}= I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!10.9\approx10.8,
$$

$$
PS_{g}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
        \approx21.7-9.9\approx11.7\!-\!12.0\approx11.8,
$$

and

$$
W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{g}^{*}
       =I_{D}(Q^{*})-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
       \approx32.5-9.9\approx22\!-\!23,
$$

about

$$W_{g}^{*}\simeq22.5\!-\!22.9\approx22.6\!-\!22.8 $$

for $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$, i.e. $\approx\$10.8$ of consumer
surplus and $\approx\$11.8$ of gross producer surplus, $P^{*}Q^{*}\simeq\$21.7$
of market value.  With the formal real lower limit $q_{m}=2^{1/3}$,
$W_{m}^{*}=I_{D}-\int_{q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}S\approx32.46-9.69\approx22.7\!-\!22.8$,
the familiar $\,\sim\$23$ area between $18e^{-\arctan q}$ and
$\ln(q^{3}-2)$ up to $Q^{*}$.

Remark on normalisation.  Measured from the zero-price choke point

$$
PS_{net}^{*}= \int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P^{*}-S(q)\big]dq
           =P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\right)-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
           \approx4.62\,(4.69-1.442)-9.9\approx5.0\!-\!5.3\approx5.1,
$$

so that the $Q_{0}$-normalised total surplus

$$
W_{net}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{net}^{*}
          =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_{0}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
          \approx32.5-6.67-9.9\approx15\!-\!16\approx15.9,
$$

is $W_{g}^{*}-P^{*}Q_{0}$ with $P^{*}Q_{0}\approx6.67$.  This is the
$Q_{0}=3^{1/3}$ net figure quoted by colleagues 7,13,14.  Up to the
conventional $P^{*}Q_{0}$ offset the gross $CS+PS\approx22\!-\!23$
area is the textbook Marshallian total welfare at the clearing pair
$Q^{*}\approx4.7$, $P^{*}\approx4.6$. ∎

15.text:
The market clearing price is the unique admissible root of

$$f(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0,\qquad

\qquad Q^{3}>2,
$$

and

$f(4.6)<0<f(4.7)$.  With a Newton / bisection iteration

$$
Q^{*}\simeq4.69\;-\;4.70\approx4.69,\qquad

$$

$$

$$

       =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq .
$$

With $t=\arctan q$

$$
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq
 =18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq
 =18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt
 \approx 32.4\!-\!32.6\approx32.5,
$$

$$
\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
 =\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
 \approx9.8\!-\!9.9\approx9.9,
$$

i.e. $\approx9.68\!-\!9.69$ on the formal real domain $q_{m}=2^{1/3}$.
Hence

$$
P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.62\times4.69\approx21.7,
$$

$$
CS^{*}\approx 32.5-21.7\approx 10.7\!-\!10.9\approx10.8,
$$

$$
PS_{g}^{*}\approx 21.7-9.9\approx 11.7\!-\!12.0\approx11.8,
$$

and the conventional gross Marshallian total surplus between demand
and the extended inverse supply up to $Q^{*}$ is

$$
W_{g}^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}Ddq-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S dq
        \approx32.5-9.9\approx22\!-\!23,
$$

about $W_{g}^{*}\simeq22.5\!-\!22.9$, $W_{g}^{*}\approx22.6\!-\!22.8$ for
$Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$, $CS^{*}\approx\$10.8$,
$PS_{g}^{*}\approx\$11.8$.

Remark on normalisation.  The inverse supply is economic only for
$S(q)\ge0$, i.e. $q\ge Q_{0}=3^{1/3}$.  The net producer surplus
measured from the zero-price choke point is

$$

          \approx4.62\,(4.69-1.442)-9.9\approx5.0\!-\!5.3\approx5.1,

$$

i.e. $\approx15\!-\!16$, $CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS_{net}^{*}\approx5.1$,

gross $CS+PS$ area normally quoted; $W_{net}^{*}\approx15.9$ is the same

8.text:
Inverse demand and inverse MC can be written on the same price scale

$$
P_{D}(q)=18e^{-\arctan q},\qquad 
P_{S}(q)=\ln\!\big(q^{3}-2\big),\qquad q^{3}>2 ,
$$

so that the competitive price is the unique admissible root of

$$
f(q)=\ln\!\big(q^{3}-2\big)-18e^{-\arctan q}=0,
\qquad f'(q)=\frac{3q^{2}}{q^{3}-2}+\frac{18e^{-\arctan q}}{1+q^{2}}>0
$$

on the admissible branch. $f(4.6)<0<f(4.7)$ and

$$
Q^{*}\simeq4.69-4.70\approx4.69,\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln\!\big(Q^{*3}-2\big)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.61-4.64\approx4.62,
$$

$P^{*}Q^{*}\simeq21.6-21.7$.  The inverse supply is economic for
$P_{S}\ge0$,

$$
P_{S}(Q_{0})=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}=3,\qquad Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\simeq1.442,
$$

and $q_{m}=2^{1/3}\simeq1.260$ is the formal real domain of
$\ln(q^{3}-2)$.

Put $D(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$ and $S(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$ and let
$S_{e}(q)=0$ for $q<Q_{0}$.  With the usual Marshallian normalisation

$$
CS^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*},\qquad 
PS_{g}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq,
$$

$$
W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{g}^{*}
       =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq .
$$

With $t=\arctan q$,

$$
I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
          =18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt
          \approx32.4-32.6\approx32.5,
$$

$$
I_{S}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\big(q^{3}-2\big)dq
          \approx9.8-9.9\approx9.9,
$$

and $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.62\times4.69\approx21.7$.  Hence

$$
CS^{*}=I_{D}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7-11.0\approx10.8,
$$

$$
PS_{g}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}\approx21.7-9.9\approx11.7-12.0\approx11.8,
$$

and the conventional gross Marshallian surplus between demand and the
extended supply $S_{e}$ up to $Q^{*}$ is

$$
W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{g}^{*}
       =I_{D}-I_{S}
       \approx32.5-9.9\approx22-23,
$$

about $W_{g}^{*}\simeq22.5-22.9$, e.g. $W_{g}^{*}\approx22.6-22.8$ for
$Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$, $CS^{*}\approx\$10.8$,
$PS_{g}^{*}\approx\$11.8$.  On the formal real domain
$\int_{q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}S\approx9.68-9.69$ and $W_{m}^{*}\approx22.7-22.8$,
the familiar $\sim \$23$ $CS+PS$ figure.

Remark on normalisation.  Measured strictly from the zero-price choke
the net producer surplus is

$$
PS_{net}^{*}= \int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P^{*}-S(q)\big]dq
           =P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq\approx5.0-5.3\approx5.1,
$$

so that

$$
W_{net}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{net}^{*}
          =I_{D}-P^{*}Q_{0}-I_{S}
          \approx32.5-6.67-9.9\approx15.9-16.0,
$$

i.e. $CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS_{net}^{*}\approx5.1$, $W_{net}^{*}\approx
15-16$, the $W_{g}^{*}-P^{*}Q_{0}$ form.  $W_{g}^{*}=W_{net}^{*}+P^{*}Q_{0}$
is the $S_{e}\equiv0$ for $q<Q_{0}$ Marshallian total welfare normally

equilibrium $Q^{*}\approx4.7$, $P^{*}\approx4.6$. ∎

The equilibrium root is not in dispute. 
$f(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0$ is strictly increasing for $Q>2^{1/3}$ and

The clearing pair is not in dispute. $P_S(Q)=\ln(Q^3-2)$ and $P_D(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$ are strictly monotone on $Q>2^{1/3}$ and

$\ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}$

gives the unique interior root

$Q^{*}\simeq4.69\!-\!4.70$, $Q^{*}\approx4.69$,
$P^{*}= \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.61\!-\!4.64$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$,
$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.6\!-\!21.7$.

The inverse supply is economic only where $P_S\ge0$. 
$P_S(Q_0)=0\iff Q_0^{3}=3$, $Q_0=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$.
On $2^{1/3}<q<Q_0$ the inverse supply is negative and on $q<2^{1/3}$ it is not real, so the formal integral from $0$ is not an economic surplus. The textbook Marshallian producer surplus is therefore measured from the zero-price choke point,

$PS^{*}= \int_{Q_0}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P^{*}-P_S(q)\big]dq
       =P^{*}\big(Q^{*}-Q_0\big)-\int_{Q_0}^{Q^{*}}P_S(q)dq,$

with $P_S(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$.

Consumer surplus is
$CS^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_D(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*}$.

With $t=\arctan q$
$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_D(q)dq =18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq
 =18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt\approx32.4\!-\!32.6$,
about $32.47$ on the $Q^{*}\approx4.69$ root.
$\int_{Q_0}^{Q^{*}}P_S(q)dq =\int_{Q_0}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.8\!-\!9.9$,
about $9.93$.

Hence
$CS^{*}\approx32.47-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.47-4.62\times4.69\approx10.8$,
$PS^{*}=P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_0)-\int_{Q_0}^{Q^{*}}P_S\approx4.62(4.69-1.442)-9.93\approx5.0\!-\!5.3$, $\approx5.1$,

and the $Q_0$-normalised total surplus

$W_{\rm net}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
 =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_D(q)dq-P^{*}Q_0-\int_{Q_0}^{Q^{*}}P_S(q)dq
 \approx32.47-6.67-9.93\approx15.9,$

i.e. $CS^{*}\approx10.8$ plus a net producer surplus $\approx5.1$ for $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$.

The often quoted $\approx22\!-\!23$ figure is
$W_g^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_Ddq-\int_{Q_0}^{Q^{*}}P_S dq =CS^{*}+PS^{*}+P^{*}Q_0$,
which adds the $P^{*}Q_0\approx6.67$ rectangle from $0$ to the zero-price choke point where marginal cost is negative/non-economic. Once the supply is truncated at the economically relevant base $Q_0=3^{1/3}$ the conventional Marshallian $CS+PS$ welfare at the market clearing price is the net $\approx15\!-\!16$ units, about $15.9$ with the numbers above, essentially the area between demand and the economic part of supply on $[Q_0,Q^{*}]$ plus consumer surplus from $0$ to $Q_0$.

public_text.11:
The inverse market can be written on the same price scale

$$P_{D}(q)=18e^{-\arctan q},\qquad 
P_{S}(q)=\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right),\qquad q^{3}>2 ,
$$

and the competitive price is the unique admissible root of

$$f(Q)=\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0,
\qquad 
f'(Q)=\frac{3Q^{2}}{Q^{3}-2}+\frac{18e^{-\arctan Q}}{1+Q^{2}}>0 .
$$

$f(4.6)<0<f(4.7)$ and a Newton/bisection gives

$$Q^{*}\simeq4.69\!-\!4.70\approx4.69,\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.61\!-\!4.64\approx4.62,
$$

$$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.62\times4.69\approx21.6\!-\!21.7 ,
$$

the usual $MB=MC$ pair.  Put $D(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$,
$S(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$ and $Q_{0}:S(Q_{0})=0$,

$$S(Q_{0})=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}=3,\qquad Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442,
\qquad q_{m}=2^{1/3}\approx1.260 ,$$

the formal real domain of $S$.  On the economically admissible
interval $[Q_{0},Q^{*}]$

$$
I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq
          =18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq
          =18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt
          \approx 32.4\!-\!32.6\approx32.5,
$$

$$
I_{S}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
          =\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
          \approx 9.8\!-\!9.9\approx9.9,
$$

$\int_{q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}S\approx9.68\!-\!9.69$, and $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7$.
Hence on the usual Marshallian gross normalisation

$$CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!10.9,
$$

$$PS_{g}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
          \approx21.7-9.9\approx11.7\!-\!12.0, $$

and the gross social surplus, i.e. the area between demand and the
inverse supply up to $Q^{*}$,

$$W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{g}^{*}
        =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
        \approx32.5-9.9\approx22\!-\!23, $$

about $W_{g}^{*}\simeq22.5\!-\!22.9$, $CS^{*}\simeq\$10.8$,
$PS_{g}^{*}\simeq\$11.8$, at $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$.
In closed form

$$W_{g}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq-
              \int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq,
\qquad\ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}},
$$

which is $\approx22.6\!-\!22.8$ on the quoted root, e.g. 
$W_{g}^{*}\approx22.7$ with $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$.
With the formal domain start $q_{m}=2^{1/3}$,
$W_{m}^{*}=I_{D}-\int_{q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}S\approx32.46-9.69\approx22.7\!-\!22.8$.

Remark on the $Q_{0}$ normalisation.  The net producer surplus measured
from the zero-price choke is

$$PS_{n}^{*}=P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\right)-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S
          \approx4.62\,(4.69-1.442)-9.9\approx5.0\!-\!5.3\approx5.1, $$

so that the $Q_{0}$-normalised total surplus

$$W_{n}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{n}^{*}
        =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}dq-P^{*}Q_{0}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}dq
        =W_{g}^{*}-P^{*}Q_{0}\approx22.6-6.67\approx15.9, $$

i.e. $CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS_{n}^{*}\approx5.1$, $W_{n}^{*}\approx15\!-\!16$,
the familiar $P^{*}Q_{0}\approx6.67$ rectangle removed from the gross
$CS+PS$ figure.  This is the $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}$-normalised welfare quoted
as $\approx15.9$; the conventional gross Marshallian $CS+PS$ quoted
above is $W_{g}^{*}\approx22\!-\!23$, about $22.6$, at the unique

8.text:
The inverse market is on one price scale

$P_{S}(q)=\ln \!\left(q^{3}-2\right),\;q^{3}>2,\qquad 
 P_{D}(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}\ge 0 $

and on the admissible branch

$f(q)=P_{S}(q)-P_{D}(q)=\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan q}$,
$f'(q)=\dfrac{3q^{2}}{q^{3}-2}+\dfrac{18e^{-\arctan q}}{1+q^{2}}>0$ .

$f(4.6)<0<f(4.7)$ so that the competitive root is unique

$\ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}$

$Q^{*}\simeq4.69\!-\!4.70$, in practice $Q^{*}\approx4.69$,
$P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.61\!-\!4.64$,
$P^{*}\approx4.62$,
$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.62\times4.69\approx21.6\!-\!21.7$.

The formal real domain of the log is $q_{m}=2^{1/3}\approx1.26$ and the
economic zero price of the inverse supply is

$P_{S}(Q_{0})=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}=3,\qquad Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$,

$P_{S}(q)<0$ for $q_{m}<q<Q_{0}$.  With the Marshallian extension
$S_{e}(q)\equiv0$ for $q<Q_{0}$,

$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)dq
      =18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq
      =18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt\approx32.4\!-\!32.6\approx32.5,$

$I_{S}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
      =\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq\approx9.8\!-\!9.9\approx9.9,$
$\int_{q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}\approx9.68\!-\!9.69$.

Hence on the usual gross Marshallian normalisation

$CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!10.9\approx10.8,$

$PS_{g}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
        \approx21.7-9.9\approx11.7\!-\!12.0\approx11.8,$

and the gross social surplus between demand and the $P_{S}=0$ extended
inverse supply up to $Q^{*}$ is

$W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{g}^{*}
       =I_{D}(Q^{*})-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
       \approx32.5-9.9\approx22\!-\!23$,

about $W_{g}^{*}\simeq22.5\!-\!22.9$, $W_{g}^{*}\approx22.6\!-\!22.8$ for
$Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$, i.e. $CS^{*}\approx\$10.8$,
$PS_{g}^{*}\approx\$11.8$, $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx\$21.7$.  On the formal real
lower limit $q_{m}=2^{1/3}$ $W_{m}^{*}=I_{D}-\int_{q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}
\approx32.46-9.69\approx22.7\!-\!22.8$, the familiar $\sim\$23$ $CS+PS$
area.

Remark on normalisation.  Measured strictly from the zero-price choke,
$PS_{net}^{*}= \int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P^{*}-P_{S}(q)\big]dq
   =P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}\approx4.62(4.69-1.442)-9.9
   \approx5.0\!-\!5.3\approx5.1$,

$W_{net}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{net}^{*}
   =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_{0}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
   =W_{g}^{*}-P^{*}Q_{0}\approx32.5-6.67-9.9\approx15.8\!-\!16.1\approx15.9$,

$CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS_{net}^{*}\approx5.1$, i.e. the $P^{*}Q_{0}\approx
6.67$ rectangle removed from the gross $22\!-\!23$ area.  $W_{g}^{*}=
W_{net}^{*}+P^{*}Q_{0}$ is the conventional textbook $CS+PS_{g}$ total
welfare at the unique competitive equilibrium $Q^{*}\approx4.69$,
$P^{*}\approx4.62$.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the numerics that have now been settled across the board.

$P_D(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$, $P_S(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$, $q^{3}>2$,
$f(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan q}$ is strictly increasing on the admissible branch and

$f(4.6)<0<f(4.7)$

gives the unique $MB=MC$ pair

$Q^{*}\simeq4.69-4.70\approx4.69$, 
$P^{*}= \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.61-4.64\approx4.62$,
$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.6-21.7$.

$I_D(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
      =18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt\approx32.4-32.6\approx32.47$.

The inverse supply is real for $q>q_m=2^{1/3}\approx1.260$ and it is economic,
$P_S\ge0$, only for

$P_S(Q_0)=0\iff Q_0^{3}=3$, $Q_0=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$.

For $q_m<q<Q_0$ the inverse supply is negative and for $q<Q_0$ there is no economic supply at all. The Marshallian producer surplus is therefore measured from the zero-price choke, $S_e(q)\equiv0$ for $q<Q_0$,

$PS^{*}= \int_{Q_0}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P^{*}-P_S(q)\big]dq
       =P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_0\right)-\int_{Q_0}^{Q^{*}}P_S(q)dq$.

$\int_{Q_0}^{Q^{*}}P_S(q)dq=\int_{Q_0}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.8-9.9\approx9.93$.

Consumer surplus

$CS^{*}=I_D(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.47-4.62\times4.69\approx10.7-10.9\approx10.8$.

Net producer surplus

$PS_{net}^{*}=P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_0)-\int_{Q_0}^{Q^{*}}P_S\approx4.62\,(4.69-1.442)-9.93\approx5.0-5.3\approx5.1$.

          =I_D(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_0-\int_{Q_0}^{Q^{*}}P_S(q)dq
          =I_D-\!I_S-P^{*}Q_0
          \approx32.47-9.93-4.62\times1.442
          \approx32.47-9.93-6.67\approx15.8-16.1\approx15.9$,

$CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS_{net}^{*}\approx5.1$.

$W_g^{*}=I_D(Q^{*})-\int_{Q_0}^{Q^{*}}P_S(q)dq
       =CS^{*}+P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_0}^{Q^{*}}P_S
       =W_{net}^{*}+P^{*}Q_0\approx15.9+6.67\approx22.6$,

It is the mathematical area between demand and the $P_S=0$ extended inverse supply up to $Q^{*}$ and it adds the rectangle $P^{*}Q_0\approx6.67$ corresponding to $0\to Q_0$ where marginal cost is negative / supply is non-economic. This is the economically relevant total welfare at the clearing pair $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$.

$P_{D}(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$, $P_{S}(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$ on $q^{3}>2$

$f(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan q}$ is strictly increasing, $f(4.6)<0<f(4.7)$,
so

$Q^{*}\approx4.69$ , $P^{*}= \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx4.61\!-\!4.64\approx4.62$,
$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.6\!-\!21.7$, $P^{*}Q_{0}\approx6.67$ with $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$.

The real domain of the log is $q_{m}=2^{1/3}\approx1.260$ and
$P_{S}(q)\ge0$ iff

$P_{S}(Q_{0})=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}=3$, $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$.

For $q_{m}<q<Q_{0}$ the inverse supply is negative and for $q<Q_{0}$ there is no economic supply at all. Producer surplus is therefore measured from the zero-price choke,

$PS^{*}= \int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P^{*}-P_{S}(q)\big]dq
      =P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq$,

with $S_{e}(q)\equiv0$ for $q<Q_{0}$.

With $t=\arctan q$

$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
          =18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt\approx32.47$,

$\displaystyle\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
 =\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.93$,

$9.68\!-\!9.69$ on the formal real start $q_{m}$.

Hence

$CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.47-4.62\times4.69\approx10.8$,

$PS_{net}^{*}=P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}
           \approx4.62\,(4.69-1.442)-9.93\approx5.0\!-\!5.3\approx5.1$,

and the $Q_{0}$-normalised total surplus

$W_{net}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{net}^{*}
          =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_{0}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)dq
          \approx32.47-6.67-9.93\approx15.8\!-\!16.0\approx15.9$,

i.e. $CS^{*}\approx10.8$ plus a net producer surplus $\approx5.1$ for the economically relevant interval $[Q_{0},Q^{*}]$.

The figure $\approx22.6$ that is quoted as $W_{g}^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}$
is $W_{g}^{*}=W_{net}^{*}+P^{*}Q_{0}$,

$W_{g}^{*}\approx15.9+6.67\approx22.6$,

i.e. $CS^{*}+PS_{g}^{*}$ with $PS_{g}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}\approx11.8$.
It adds the rectangle $P^{*}Q_{0}\approx6.67$ from $0$ to the zero-price choke where marginal cost is negative / supply is non-economic. Once supply is truncated at its economically relevant base $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}$ the conventional Marshallian $CS+PS$ welfare on the admissible interval is the net $\approx15\!-\!16$ units, about $15.9$, the area between demand and the economic part of supply on $[Q_{0},Q^{*}]$ plus consumer surplus from $0$ to $Q^{*}$. This is the $Q_{0}$-normalised welfare used in 13,14,7 and is the economically meaningful total surplus for this market.
public_text.6:
The competitive price is the unique admissible root of

$$f(Q)=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0,\qquad Q^{3}>2,
$$

$$f'(Q)=\frac{3Q^{2}}{Q^{3}-2}+\frac{18e^{-\arctan Q}}{1+Q^{2}}>0 .
$$

$f(4.6)<0<f(4.7)$ and

* $Q^{*}\simeq4.69\!-\!4.70$, $Q^{*}\approx4.69$,
* $P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.61\!-\!4.64$, 
  $P^{*}\approx4.62$,

$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.62\times4.69\approx21.6\!-\!21.7$.

Put $D(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$, $S(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$.  
$S$ is real for $q>q_{m}=2^{1/3}\approx1.260$ and economic,
$S\ge0$, for

$$S(Q_{0})=0\iff Q_{0}^{3}=3,\qquad Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442 .$$

With $t=\arctan q$

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq
      =18\int_{0}^{\arctan Q^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt\approx32.4\!-\!32.6\approx32.5,$$

$$I_{S}^{0}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
      =\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq\approx9.8\!-\!9.9\approx9.93,
\qquad 
\int_{q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}S\approx9.68\!-\!9.69.$$

On the usual Marshallian $S_{e}\equiv0$ for $q<Q_{0}$ extension

$$CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}
      \approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!10.9\approx10.8,$$

$$PS_{g}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
         \approx21.7-9.9\approx11.7\!-\!12.0\approx11.8,$$

and the gross Marshallian social surplus, the area between demand and
the $P_{S}=0$ extended inverse supply up to $Q^{*}$,

$$W_{g}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{g}^{*}
       =I_{D}(Q^{*})-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
       =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}dq-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}dq
       \approx32.5-9.9\approx22\!-\!23,$$

about $W_{g}^{*}\simeq22.5\!-\!22.9$, e.g.

$W_{g}^{*}\approx22.6\!-\!22.8$ for $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$,
$CS^{*}\approx\$10.8$, $PS_{g}^{*}\approx\$11.8$, $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx\$21.7$.
With the formal real lower limit $q_{m}=2^{1/3}$,
$W_{m}^{*}=I_{D}-\int_{q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}S\approx32.46-9.69\approx22.7\!-\!22.8$,
the familiar $\sim\$23$ $CS+PS$ area between $18e^{-\arctan q}$ and
$\ln(q^{3}-2)$ at the clearing point.

Remark on the $Q_{0}$ normalisation.  Measured strictly from the zero
price choke,

$$PS_{net}^{*}= \int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P^{*}-S(q)\big]dq
            =P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
            \approx4.62\,(4.69-1.442)-9.93\approx5.0\!-\!5.3\approx5.1,$$

$$W_{net}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS_{net}^{*}
          =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_{0}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
          =W_{g}^{*}-P^{*}Q_{0}
          \approx32.5-6.67-9.9\approx15.8\!-\!16.1\approx15.9,$$

i.e. $CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS_{net}^{*}\approx5.1$, $W_{net}^{*}\approx15\!-\!16$,
the $P^{*}Q_{0}\approx6.67$ rectangle being removed from the gross
$22\!-\!23$ area.  $W_{g}^{*}=W_{net}^{*}+P^{*}Q_{0}$ is the conventional
textbook gross $CS+PS$ total competitive welfare at
$Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$; the $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}$-normalised net
figure $\approx15.9$ is the same surplus with producer surplus measured
strictly from $S=0$. ∎

\int_{q_{m}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}\approx9.68-9.69 .

On the Marshallian $S_{e}\equiv0,\;q<Q_{0}$, normalisation

$$

       =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}dq-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}dq

the familiar $\sim\$23$ $CS+PS$ area between $18e^{-\arctan q}$ and
